scope: Uncommitted working-tree efficiency roadmap after the direct-upload pass. Dense 4K viewport payload and exact pixel checks, optional-job scheduling, cache lookup and asset fingerprint changes, latency diagnostics and contextual brush editing. CPU and texture payload evidence, not physical pen latency, GPU commitment, total RSS or a fixed global memory cap.

viewport_residency.scope: Dense patterned artwork, production workers, coherent publication checked on every update, sampled tiles compared with independent image-library reduction. Payload only, not physical VRAM; source/compositor memory excluded. Visible resolution follows screen density; no fixed global cap for arbitrarily large/high-DPI viewports. One run, not pen latency.

moving_display_scope: Supported 512/2048 documents, one dense flat/tiled base and sparse extra layers. 24 opaque region changes with one paint and one idle display update per change, followed by an 8 ms sleep. A center marker reports logical input-update age and same-call visibility; not physical tablet latency, UI frame rate or GPU rendering. Initial upload/setup, writes/COW, validation and sleep excluded from owner timings. Production workers are used. Final padded pixels and input-update payload accounting verified. One sequential run per case; no statistical speedup or hard deadline claim.

render_queue.allocation_scope: Common registry samples live document, retained history and active stroke/fill settlement after each owner advance. Shared pixel allocations count once; settlement includes embedded snapshot metadata, partial raw copying, prepared Arc patch buffers, region-vector and fill-plan capacities. Peaks for separate fields may occur at different calls and must not be added. Sampling is outside owner timing but inside drain wall, can miss short-lived settlement, and excludes emitted snapshots, other active stroke/fill buffers, worker scratch/output, descriptor/registry bookkeeping and allocator overhead. This is not RSS or a global memory budget.
render_queue.scope: Supported 512-square empty tiled and 2048-square dense single-layer raster documents in both flat compatibility and tiled storage. Profiling is enabled for per-unit phase counts/timings and adds clock overhead. Two overlapping timestamped strokes, completed-stroke snapshot, undo snapshot, redo and document fence. CPU advance timings include checkpoint/settlement/reclamation, undo/redo and snapshot control units; full pixel checks are outside each call timer, inside total wall. Input generation and reference painting precede all timers. A two-millisecond deadline is checked between units, with a 32-unit cap; synchronous controls and individual rows can overrun it. Rollback-only timings cover cancellation cursor construction, original row restoration, incremental scratch release, tile reclamation and final checkpoint discard/accounting; they exclude preparation/live painting and final pixel verification. Rollback must restore every pixel of both completed strokes. Settlement scans and copies one tile row per unit, retaining the full checkpoint until atomic publication; final trimming/accounting and buffer release remain synchronous. Settlement payload peak estimates count partial region buffers and region-vector capacity, excluding shared snapshot pixels, metadata clones, allocator overhead and stack fields. Input bytes exclude active buffers/history/snapshots, vacant queue capacity and allocator overhead. An additional typed-command correctness sequence runs after all reported timers: invalid target, reserved-identity new layer, identity-target rename, opacity, captured-identity stroke and snapshot, checking both layers in full against synchronous reference output. Typed raster commands and their history settlement remain synchronous; legacy target indices remain execution-relative; new identity targets survive reorder and reject missing layers. Drains without UI waits; does not measure driver/UI/display or save filesystem commits.
render_queue.stroke_scope: Exclusive active stroke buffers and cursors are sampled outside owner-call timing, inside drain wall: remaining original/coverage blocks, vector capacities, prefix/tail storage, cursor payload and rollback key-table entries. Excludes map control bytes and shared captured Settings. Finished prefix/tail allocations retire incrementally during compaction while original pixels remain available for rollback. Released bytes record those work units; remaining scratch may drop at completion. Separate peaks must not be added: the combined tracked field samples live, history, settlement and stroke together. Sampling can miss short-lived states; excludes emitted snapshots, fill working buffers, worker scratch/output, descriptor/registry bookkeeping and allocator overhead. Not RSS or a global memory budget.

limitations: Viewport probe is one release run; moving display has three alternating trials per binary, descriptive medians only.
Moving-display benchmark does not set a viewport and isolates existing small-region/cache behavior. The separate dense 4K probe exercises adaptive display resolution.
Reduced tiles currently rebuild through background preparation when edited; immediate subuploads apply to full-detail tiles.
Large previews carry their own display plan. Previous generations and parked projects add retained data.
Existing background workers are not preempted. Quiet-period rules govern admission only.
Physical tablet, sustained GPU and total memory measurements remain separate acceptance checks.

moving_display_comparison.scope: Median accumulated owner time across 48 input/idle calls for 24 edits. Three trials per binary. No viewport: this measures existing full-detail display behavior, not adaptive texture residency.
moving_display_comparison.interpretation: This pass does not establish a net CPU display speedup. Retained texture payload is the clear measured improvement; scheduling and cached asset hashes address separate work.
